title: PIM Is All You Need: A CXL-Enabled GPU-Free System for Large Language Model Inference
problem: LLM inference is memory-bound (GEMV-dominated decoding stage with ~21% GPU compute utilization on Llama2-70B), yet modern GPU/TPU systems are optimized for compute throughput; simultaneously, large KV-cache requirements per user limit batch sizes, and CXL- or DRAM-density-reduced PIM architectures individually lack sufficient memory capacity or scalability for trillion-parameter LLMs.
motivation: Running Llama2-70B on 4x A100 GPUs costs ~$694K/day for ChatGPT-scale inference while compute utilization remains below 25%, driving the need for memory-bandwidth-optimized, cost-efficient alternatives as LLM parameter sizes scale toward trillion parameters.
method: CENT uses a hierarchical processing-in-memory (PIM) and near-memory (PNM) architecture deployed across 32 GDDR6-PIM memory devices connected via CXL 3.0. Each PIM device contains 16 multiply-accumulate units (32 billion operations per second in BF16), handling over 99% of the arithmetic, plus PNM units with 32 accumulators, reduction trees, special hardware for exponential functions, and 8 CPU cores for operations like Softmax (attention probability calculation), RMSNorm (normalization), square roots, and RoPE (rotary embeddings). A custom instruction set with commands like MAC_ABK (for matrix operations) and BCAST_CXL (for broadcasting) orchestrates computation and data movement across the CXL network. Pipeline parallelism assigns each transformer layer to one device with multiple prompts flowing through in sequence, while tensor parallelism splits a transformer layer across all devices synchronized via CXL broadcast and gather, with a hybrid mode for balancing throughput and responsiveness.
key_novelty: CENT replaces GPUs with a hierarchical PIM-PNM system connected via CXL 3.0 with a novel broadcast primitive, leveraging GDDR6-PIM's 512 trillion bytes per second internal bandwidth to achieve 2.3x higher LLM inference throughput than 4x A100 GPUs at 2.9x lower energy and 5.2x better TCO.
contributions: CENT: a GPU-free hierarchical PIM-PNM architecture over 32 CXL devices supporting full transformer block computation with 512 TB/s aggregate internal memory bandwidth.
Scalable CXL network with novel broadcast/multicast primitives via reserved H-slot flit encoding, enabling collective and peer-to-peer communication across up to 4,096 CXL nodes.

Mapping of LLM parallelism strategies (PP, TP, hybrid TP-PP) onto the CXL-PIM network with detailed transformer block operation assignment (GEMV to PIM, Softmax/RMSNorm/RoPE to PNM RISC-V/accelerators).
2.3x throughput and 2.9x energy efficiency over 4x A100 GPUs at similar average power; 5.2x tokens per dollar; 4.6x latency reduction in latency-critical (batch=1) mode.

metrics.speedup: 2.3x end-to-end throughput over 4x A100 80GB GPUs (throughput-critical); 4.6x latency reduction (batch=1); 3.3x decoding throughput at 32K context
metrics.area: CXL controller: 19.0 mm2 at 7nm; custom logic: 7.85 mm2 at 28nm
metrics.other: 5.2x tokens per dollar (TCO); CENT owned TCO $0.73/hr vs GPU $1.76/hr; rental TCO $1.05/hr vs $5.45/hr

baselines: 4x NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU with NVLink 3.0 running vLLM (batch=128)
limitations: CENT underperforms GPU by 2x in the compute-intensive prefill stage due to lower peak FLOPS; current evaluation limited to Llama2 (7B/13B/70B) at up to 32K context; near-bank PIM memory density reduced to ~75% of standard GDDR6.
primary_theme: CXL-scaled PIM-PNM architecture for GPU-free LLM inference
